# Multiplayer

@difference Multiplayer uses TCP on port 40500 instead of DirectPlay, so games only play with other BlitzLLVM games.

The multiplayer commands (`StartNetGame`, `HostNetGame`, `JoinNetGame`, `StopNetGame`, `CreateNetPlayer`, `DeleteNetPlayer`, `SendNetMsg`, `RecvNetMsg` and the rest) used DirectPlay in the originals, which is no longer available. In BlitzLLVM the programs that join a game connect to the program that hosts it over TCP, on port 40500. The host passes messages on to the other programs.

* Games made with BlitzLLVM can only play with other games made with BlitzLLVM. They can not join, or be joined by, a program made with Blitz3D.
* Every package on a connection, whichever kind, is at most 64 KB. A message for `SendNetMsg` can therefore carry at most 65526 bytes of data, and `SendNetMsg` gives 0 for a bigger one without sending it. A program that sends a bigger package over a connection is disconnected. The same goes for a program that keeps sending while the other side does not call `RecvNetMsg`: once more than 64 KB of its messages are waiting, its connection is closed, and its players are gone for the others (the host sees them leave, a program that joined gets the message that the session was lost).
* The port can be changed with the environment variable `BLITZLLVM_NETGAME_PORT`. Every program of a game has to use the same one, and the host needs it to be open in its firewall.
* `StartNetGame` shows a dialog that asks whether to host or to join. When joining, the address of the host is asked on the console.
* The environment variable `BLITZLLVM_DIALOG_ANSWER` presses a button of a dialog without showing it (0 is the first button), which is meant for automated runs. It answers `RequestFont` and `RequestColor` the same way: 0 accepts what they start with, anything else cancels them.
